newsitem.title: UK: London freight - BFI slumps another 18 points.
newsitem.headline: London freight - BFI slumps another 18 points.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) slumped anther 18 points to 1,314, as brokers found a scarcity of employment for vessels.
However, some scope for hope was noted from an increase in enquiry and the continued steadiness indicated for a prompt U.S. Gulf/Japan heavy grain shipment at $22.

One problem cited behind the recent weakness of the dry cargo freight market, was the extreme weather pattern in the U.S. Gulf, which brokers said had been very unhelpful, but now that the weather seems to have settled in that region, maybe the market will prove to have bottomed out.
"I think as the Greek influence on the shipping market is considerable, the market will remain quiet until next week, as orthodox Greek's observance of Easter takes hold," one said.
Little fresh fixing on any major grain route was reported apart from Italgrani, who fixed 35,000 tonnes of wheat from Nopac to south Spain end May at $20.25.

On the mineral sector, no new capesize business was reported for coal cargoes, but a few were seen for ore. Amngst those were, BHP who booked 150,000 tonnes ore Port Hedland/Redcar and Immingham 1-15/6 at $8.30-$8.40 and BSC for 150,000 tonnes ore Cape Lambert/Redcar 3-10/5 at $8.10.
Timecharter business was also slow, with very little fixing of either capesizes or panamaxes.
Amongst the few capesizes that were taken on a timecharter basis was the Folegandros 127,209 dwt by Brade Carriers del China end May trip W.Australia round trip at $10,000 daily.
While on the panamax side, the Maratha Mighty 72,870 dwt was fixed by NSAC del Plate 6-14/5 trip and redel Far East for $12,500 daily plus a $230,000 ballast bonus.
The BIFFEX futures closed five to 25 points below Monday's finish. Most active May traded last at 1,290, down 25. May volume was 308 lots, while total volume ammounted to 693 lots.
